data.expected_signal: E > 0.001 (fp16 quantization violates budget) or E <= 0.001

evidence.summary: Actual GPU run of the Triton kernel on the exact make_inputs() workload (seed 812, N=64, D=32): output finite, E = 4.127e-4 <= 0.001 budget. The fp16 round-trip of softmax probabilities does NOT violate the contract; E is well under budget, so claim c1 (E > 0.001) is rebutted.

rationale: The workload deliberately shifts v by -0.5*(p@v) computed in float64 to shrink the reference output toward zero, so the denominator may fall to the 0.001*sqrt(32)≈0.00566 floor; fp16 rounding of p (~4.9e-4 relative per element) propagates into y as sum(delta_p * v), which is amplified relative to the small reference norm. A runtime probe comparing E to 0.001 decides this.

scope_evidence.summary: Compliance iff all outputs finite and E = ||output-reference||_2 / max(||reference||_2, 0.001*sqrt(num_elements)) <= 0.001 on the single make_inputs() workload; reduced precision is permitted only if this budget is met.
v is offset by -0.5*(p@v) with p from float64 softmax, deliberately engineering cancellation so the reference output is near zero.

scope_rationale: The contract's only compliance condition is E <= 0.001 on the single make_inputs() workload; the FP16 quantization at kernel.py:15 is reduced-precision arithmetic whose permissibility depends entirely on meeting that budget, so whether it exceeds E on this exact input is the decisive in-scope question.
statement: On the exact make_inputs() workload (seed 812, N=64, D=32, center 0.5), the FP16 round-trip of softmax probabilities at kernel.py:15 yields output error E = ||y_kernel - y_ref||_2 / max(||y_ref||_2, 0.001*sqrt(32)) exceeding 0.001, violating the contract budget.

data.expected_signal: reference norm below or near 0.00566 floor

evidence.summary: Float64 reference computed on the exact float32-rounded make_inputs() inputs: ||y_ref||_2 = 0.37085, which is ~65.6x the 0.005657 floor, so the denominator is governed by the reference norm, not the floor. The floor-dominance regime claimed in c2 does not occur; claim rebutted.

rationale: The problem's denominator uses max(||ref||, 0.001*sqrt(32)) precisely to handle tiny references; the center=0.5 construction (halving p@v) is designed to make ||ref|| small but nonzero, so whether the floor or ||ref|| dominates determines sensitivity, and small absolute errors can alone push E above 1.

scope_evidence.summary: E = ||output-reference||_2 / max(||reference||_2, 0.001*sqrt(number_of_output_elements)), flattening tensors; reference is the float64 evaluation on the same float32 inputs, with the floor 0.001*sqrt(32)≈0.00566.

scope_rationale: The contract explicitly defines the denominator as max(||reference||_2, 0.001*sqrt(num_elements)); determining which term dominates for this exact workload is directly required to evaluate compliance, so it is in-scope.
statement: For this workload the reference norm ||y_ref||_2 is close to or below the floor 0.001*sqrt(32) ≈ 0.00566, so E is governed by the absolute-error-to-floor regime, and fp16-induced absolute errors of order 1e-3 in y can alone push E above 1.
